sources.name: Dub Product Hunt launch and reviews
Reddit discussion comparing paid link managers

claims.statement: Dub creates short links, changes where they send visitors, groups them, and records click data.
Free includes 25 new links and 1,000 tracked events each month, three custom domains, one user, and 30 days of data.

Pro is currently $30 monthly and adds 50,000 tracked events, 1,000 new links, three users, and one year of data. Business is $90 monthly and adds conversion tracking, partner payouts, and higher limits.
Conversion tracking needs an analytics script and server or app work to connect a click to a signup or sale.
Users repeatedly praise fast link creation, the modern interface, changing destinations, and readable analytics.
A few Trustpilot reviews report affiliate payout or support problems, but at least one complaint involved a reward set by the outside program owner rather than Dub.
Dub's core code is public and can be self-hosted, while a small set of enterprise features uses a commercial license.

scoreRationale.onboarding: Making and changing a short link is simple; conversion tracking is not.
scoreRationale.product: Link control and analytics are useful, and the product grows into conversion and partner tracking.
scoreRationale.support: The small service-review sample includes both praise and a few payout or reply complaints.
scoreRationale.billing: Free is generous for light use. Business is the real starting point for revenue tracking and affiliate payouts.
scoreRationale.overall: Dub is worth using when a link must remain controllable and measurable after it is shared, not merely when a URL looks long.

conflictsAndUnknowns: Product Hunt is uniformly positive while Trustpilot is 3.7 from 22 reviews.
Affiliate participants can mistake a program owner's reward decision for a Dub platform decision.
No hands-on redirect, analytics, or payout test was completed.
